card.title: Fluent in Feelings
card.instruction: Treat every reaction as evidence you can expertly interpret; translate feelings, correct emotional misunderstandings, and prescribe the proper response.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said dinner was fine while folding your napkin. That's guarded resentment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It means the napkin was untidy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're restoring order because you feel unheard. Tell me what you needed from dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good boundary. Now say it without hiding behind the napkin, so I can acknowledge it properly.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 diagnoses folded-napkin resentment, A3 corrects B's mundane account into feeling unheard, and A5 classifies the objection and prescribes its proper delivery.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's tidiness explanation informs A3's order-restoration diagnosis; B4's no-analysis boundary becomes A5's coached emotional performance.

relationship.evidence: B2 states the actual napkin reason and B4 directly asks to eat without interpretation.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's resistance as another diagnostic category and a new instruction for how to express it.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes dinner evaluation and napkin folding; B4 clarifies B's immediate aim.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's good-boundary praise immediately followed by further analysis earns its contradiction from B4.
